statements.status_notes: PulseCheck does not call PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex(), PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(), PEM_X509_INFO_read(), or PEM_X509_INFO_read_ex() with a caller-supplied existing X509_INFO stack. The production dependency set is requirements.txt; cryptography is a development-only dependency in requirements-dev.txt and is not installed by Dockerfile.dhi. The inspected production application has no custom PEM/X509 stack handling. The vulnerable condition requires reuse of a pre-existing non-NULL stack after a failed read. This assessment is limited to the exact OpenSSL package versions listed. Reassess if custom PEM/X509 parsing or additional cryptographic bindings are introduced.

PulseCheck uses Python's standard TLS implementation through Uvicorn and httpx.AsyncClient. The application does not enable DANE, configure TLSA records, or call OpenSSL DANE APIs. The vulnerable condition requires a DANE-enabled TLS client processing particular TLSA and certificate combinations. DANE processing is therefore not in the PulseCheck application execution path. Reassess if DANE or custom OpenSSL TLSA functionality is introduced.

PulseCheck does not parse or verify CMS/PKCS#7 SignedData, does not call CMS_verify() or PKCS7_verify(), and does not enable CRL checking for CMS/PKCS#7 verification. Its HTTP and HTTPS functionality uses the standard TLS certificate-validation path, not CMS SignedData verification. The vulnerable execution path is not used by the PulseCheck application. Reassess if CMS/PKCS#7 verification or CRL-enabled SignedData processing is introduced.
